title: FTS silent failure costs 130x on the most common query path
evidence: GQ-010-BASELINE.html §4.3. PGRT-005 reproduced and quantified: LIKE scan 222.1ms vs FTS 1.7ms.

spec.description: ask.py queries FTS with a schema-qualified table name that SQLite rejects; the OperationalError is swallowed by a bare 'except sqlite3.Error' and the code falls through to a LIKE scan. The query looks like it works. 130x slower on the graph's single most common entry point, while the FTS index is fully built, functional, and simply never reached.
spec.context: The schema comment predicted this exactly - 'measured 57ms at 36k people, and it grows linearly' - and at 339k people it is now 222ms, tracking that prediction. This is a ONE-LINE FIX and the one place a genuine, honest 80%+ retrieval-time improvement is available today. Belongs with TASK-0002 (Lane 6, which owns ask.py). Record the measured cost as the justification. Caution from the same baseline: sub-second SQL is NOT the GQ-010 bottleneck, so do not present this as satisfying criterion #4 - the real operator cost is the analyst loop around the query. Measured 2026-08-07 by PG-BASELINE against the shipped graph-v2 asset: people_graph_v2.sqlite, 1,113,350,144 bytes, db SHA-256 9938237a33277fe3a29a278d68c361a1f300d9060740cc2e917920157d9b919b, at repo commit de048bb3b34bf931b56fd741cb46c1334acdfb98.
